_readme: PEAS analysis for the 'training wheels' course level (single-robot foraging). Each field has a 'wired' flag: true means editing 'value' actually changes the simulator's behavior through edu_env.make_edu_env(); false means the field is a faithful description of the task, but there is no dial in the code you can turn to change it. This distinction is intentional -- see training_wheels/README.md for why.

performance_measure.note: Descriptive only. ForagingEnv.step() always returns reward=0.0; there is no scalar reward signal wired into the environment at this level. The utility-based agent (later module) computes its own utility from the observation/info, entirely outside the environment.

observability.note: True in the sense that each robot only sees 8 range-limited proximity sensors plus food bearing/odor -- but this is an emergent property of _get_obs_single(), not a parameter you can flip. There is no 'observability' switch in ForagingEnvConfig.

determinism.note: Sensor readings have injected Gaussian noise (see the noise injection in _get_obs_single). True, but not a single named toggle -- the noise amount is hardcoded in the environment source, not exposed as a config field.

episodic.note: Each step's observation depends on the robot's position from previous steps (a sequential environment), not just the current instant. This is a property of the physics, not something a config field controls.

dynamics.note: Whether the world changes between episodes (obstacle jitter, food/spawn location) IS controlled directly by these two boolean flags.

state_space.note: Positions and headings are floats in a continuous 2D plane. True, but again emergent, not a switch -- see the 'grid discretization' module used later for goal-based search, CSP, and Q-learning, which is a separate, explicit abstraction layer we build on top.

agents.note: This one is real: num_agents=1 for every agent type in this course level, except the predator-prey minimax module (later), which needs num_agents=2.

map.note: One of 'default', 'u_shape', 'n_shape'. Directly wired to ForagingEnvConfig.map_name.

actuators.note: Fixed action table baked into ForagingEnv._apply_action(); not configurable.

sensors.note: The social_signal channel exists in the code but is deliberately turned off at this course level (social_mode='off' in edu_env.py), so it is NOT part of this level's percept even though the underlying environment supports it.
